dedupe_keys.name: building level storm damage repair permits from municipal records hurricane harvey and hurricane ian

description: This dataset is an open, building-level record of structural storm damage taken from municipal building permits after two hurricanes: Harvey in Houston, Texas (permits 2017 to 2019) and Ian in Lee County, Cape Coral and Fort Myers, Florida (2022 to 2024). It was built by Isaiah Lyons-Galante of the University of Colorado Boulder with Virendra Dhakhada of Google, who identified storm-caused repairs with an econometric keyword-surge model and multimodal large language model review. It holds more than 174,000 high-confidence repair records (probability at least 0.90) worth over 11 billion dollars in declared valuations, each with a peril driver (flood inundation, wind and roof or tree damage, secondary repair), a standard work category, declared value, filing date, the model's justification and, for Harvey, flood depth from USGS and FEMA grids. Access: CSV and Parquet files on Zenodo, published 28 August 2026. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: addresses are replaced by block-group codes and coarse coordinates for privacy, and classification is automated. Simulation uses are calibrating hurricane damage and fragility models against observed repairs and studying recovery timelines. Related records: the Türkiye earthquake damage datasets and StEER reports.
